Welcome to the Natural Hazards Explorer!

This tool is used for exploring natural hazard risks and their impact on Utah’s transportation infrastructure.

This easy-to-use platform helps identify which natural hazards, like floods or earthquakes, are most relevant to a location.


Key Features:

• Analyze Hazards: Quickly assess the exposure of transportation assets to natural hazards.

• Interactive Maps: View and explore the prevalence of natural hazards on a map.

• Custom Location Inputs: Type in an address or upload a file to get started.

• Download Reports: Save a report with all the details needed for planning or sharing.


Ready to get started?


Follow the on-screen tool tips by clicking on the information icon.

Click “>” to navigate the quick user start guide and discover the tool's capabilities.

Quick Start Guide: Draw Tab


Analysis Pane

Use the filter pane on the left-hand side to select your location, choose an asset type, and generate a report.

  1. Choose a Location Enter an address to zoom to the area or interest.
  2. Draw your project or upload a file: Once the map focuses on the desired location, draw a shape to define the project boundaries or upload a data file. Supported file formats include Shapefile, CSV, KML, GeoJSON, and GPX.
  3. Select an Asset Pick the type of asset to analyze, such as bridges vs. pavements. This selection will generate a list of relevant hazard indicators (e.g., avalanches, debris flows, droughts) associated with the selected asset.
  4. View Risk Levels & Download Results: Click “Analyze” to generate a risk assessment for the selected asset with natural hazards.
  5. Download Results: Click “Download Report” to save a report. The report will include a full list of eight asset types (e.g., bridges, pavements, traffic signals, ITS devices, barriers, culverts, walls, overhead/multi-post signs) and their potential exposure to associated natural hazards in the selected location.
Type an address or the name of a location to set the project area. This will zoom in on the map to help define project boundaries.
Draw the boundaries of the project directly on the map or upload a file containing the project details. Supported file formats include Shapefile, CSV, KML, GeoJSON, and GPX.
3. Asset System﻿

﻿Choose the type of asset to analyze, such as bridges vs. pavements. This will generate a customized list of relevant hazard indicators (e.g., avalanches, debris flows, droughts) associated with the selected asset.


Click Analyze to view the results.


To save the results, click Download Report.
Layer List

Natural Hazards﻿

The FEMA NRI Index rates natural hazards like floods, earthquakes, and wildfires, while UDOT adds localized data for risks like rockfall, liquefaction, drainage, and erosion. These ratings are mapped to FEMA’s hazard levels (e.g., "Very High" or "Low") and are directly reflected in the map. These layer sources can be accessed here: UDOT Layers Source


Layer List Tool Tip

Customize the map view by enabling or disabling various data layers. Click the arrow (>) next to each category—Assets, Natural Hazards, or Boundaries—to expand and explore available options.

  1. Combine Filters: Apply multiple filters across categories to tailor the map. For instance, overlay bridges with flooding zones within a specific MPO for targeted insights.
  2. Dynamic Updates: Filters automatically refresh the map in real time, providing an immediate visual of the selected data.

Quick Start Guide: Draw Tab


Map Functions

  1. Zoom: Use the “+” and “−” buttons to zoom in and out of the map or scroll with the mouse for a smoother navigation experience.
  2. Home: Click the “Home” button to instantly reset the map to its original zoom level and refocus on the default view.
  3. Search Bar: Easily find an address or place by typing into the search bar.
  4. Basemap: Toggle between the default street map and satellite imagery by clicking the thumbnail in the bottom-right corner of the map.
  5. Measure: Use the Measure Tool to calculate distances or areas on the map. To begin, click the tool to activate it, then click on the map to place the starting point. Drag to the desired location and double-click to set the endpoint and complete the measurement.

Quick Start Guide: Explore Tab


The Explore Tab is the central tool for navigating and refining natural hazard exploration. Use the Explore Tab to focus on specific asset types, identify natural hazard exposure, or to narrow the view to boundaries.

  1. Refine the View with Layers: Apply multiple layers across three main categories: assets, natural hazards, and boundaries.
  2. Census-Based Precision: The tool uses 2020 census tracts to ensure localized and precise viewing. These tracts incorporate aggregated layers, including infrastructure data, natural hazard exposure, and administrative boundaries like MPOs and regions.
  3. Customize the Base Map: Toggle between a street view or satellite imagery.

Quick Start Guide: Explore Tab

Getting Started with Toggling Layers On and Off

On the right-hand side of the map is the toggle pane. Use this section to turn on or off different layers of data. Click the arrow (>) next to each category (assets, natural hazards, and Boundary) to see the available options. Select multiple options within or across categories to create a customized map view. As an example, bridges can be layered over flooding zones within a specific MPO.

Layer Categories

  1. Assets – Choose the type of infrastructure. Decide which transportation features to highlight on the map:
  2. Bridges: Explore how bridge structures interact with environmental challenges, such as floods, seismic activity, or erosion, to better understand their resilience to these hazards.
  3. Traffic Signals: Highlight the potential disruptions to traffic signals caused by natural events like extreme weather or flooding, offering insight into areas that might need closer attention.
  4. UTA Transit Stops: Discover how transit stops might be influenced by natural hazards, focusing on their accessibility and continued service for public transit users.
  5. UTA Transit Routes: Dive into how natural hazards could impact bus and rail services, shedding light on transit routes and their ability to maintain operations and connectivity during challenging conditions.
  6. Natural Hazards – See areas affected by natural events. Select from different hazard types to overlay them on the map:
  7. Flooding: Show areas prone to river or flash flooding.
  8. Wildfires: Highlight zones at risk of fire or debris flows after a fire.
  9. Seismic Activity: View regions exposed to earthquake risks.
  10. Rockfalls & Avalanches: Highlight steep or mountainous areas where these events may occur.
  11. Extreme Weather: Add layers for risks like droughts, snowstorms, or severe weather.
  12. Boundaries – Focus on specific geographic areas. Use these filters to see data by administrative or geographic regions:
  13. Metropolitan Planning Organizations (MPOs): Focus on specific transportation planning areas.
  14. County Boundaries: Limit the layers displayed to a particular county.
  15. Regions: Refine the view to focus on broader administrative divisions.
  16. Municipalities: Pinpoint data specific to cities or towns.

Quick Start Guide: Explore Tab

Map Tools

  1. Search Bar: Easily find an address or place by typing into the search bar.
  2. Layer & Legend
  3. Open the legend to toggle the “Resilience Explorer” and “Hotspot” layers on or off by clicking the eye icon next to each layer.
  4. The legend also helps understand the map’s symbology, explaining what the colors or icons represent for a clearer view of the data.
  5. Base Map: Toggle between the default street map and satellite imagery by clicking the thumbnail in the bottom-right corner of the map.

Interpreting Results from the Natural Hazards Explorer

Data Integration

The Natural Hazards Explorer combines datasets to provide a comprehensive understanding of natural hazard risks affecting Utah’s transportation infrastructure.

What’s Included:

  1. FEMA National Risk Index (NRI): This covers 12 natural hazards, such as:
  2. Avalanche, Flooding, Wildfire, Earthquake, Heat Wave, Landslide, and more.
  3. UDOT-Specific Hazard Layers: Adds localized insights on:
  4. Rockfall, Liquefaction, Drainage, and Erosion.
  5. Geographic Boundaries: Filter by MPOs, counties, regions, or municipalities.
  6. 2020 Census Tracts: Enables community-level insights.
  7. Transportation Asset Inventories: Include barriers, bridges, culverts, ITS devices, overhead/multipost signs, pavement, traffic signals, and walls.

How UDOT Data Enhances FEMA’s NRI:

  1. UDOT hazards (e.g., Rockfall, Liquefaction) were mapped to FEMA’s risk categories (e.g., "Very High" to "Very Low").
  2. Each hazard uses classifications to help compare risks.
  3. Example: Rockfall – High Hazard aligns with Relatively High Risk on the map.

Scoring and Visualization

The tool uses a scoring system ranging from 1 (low risk) to 5 (highest risk) to visualize resilience risks effectively:

  1. Hazard Exposure: Indicates the frequency, severity, and proximity of hazards to infrastructure assets.
  2. Layer Interaction: Apply multiple filters to explore overlapping risks and gather localized insights.
  3. FEMA’s NRI Hazard Ratings: Displays natural hazards (e.g., floods, wildfires) combined with UDOT’s localized data for additional risks like erosion and rockfall.
  4. Color-Coded Maps: Easily identify areas of higher or lower exposure through intuitive gradients, making vulnerabilities visually clear.
  5. Layer Customization: Toggle hazard types, geographic boundaries, and base map styles (e.g., street or satellite view) for a tailored exploration experience.

Using the Explorer for Decision-Making

Hazard Exposure:

This layer reflects the likelihood and potential impact of hazards on infrastructure. Use this data to prioritize areas for resilience planning and mitigation.

  1. Example: Filter for bridges in flood-prone zones or regions at risk of wildfires to narrow focus.

Practical Workflow:

  1. Select a Geographic Area: Choose an MPO, county, or other boundary of interest.
  2. Overlay Hazards and Assets: Combine hazard layers with transportation assets to identify specific vulnerabilities.
  3. Focus on Overlapping Risks: Use these insights to prioritize project planning and funding applications.

Hazard Examples:

  1. Rockfall: Areas classified as Very High Hazard are mapped directly to FEMA’s Very High Risk category.
  2. Liquefaction: Zones with High Susceptibility are labeled Relatively High Risk in the system.
  3. Drainage: Look for Poorly Drained Areas to identify flood-prone zones (Relatively High Risk).
  4. Erosion: Areas marked Class 3 Erosion show Very High Risk for infrastructure stability.

Methodological Alignment

The platform aligns with:

  1. UDOT’s Transportation Asset Management Plan (TAMP): Ensuring that critical infrastructure is prioritized effectively.
  2. Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) PROTECT Program Guidelines: Supporting national and state-level resilience goals.

This alignment ensures the platform provides actionable insights while maintaining consistency with established resilience frameworks, aiding planners, engineers, and decision-makers in strengthening Utah’s transportation systems.
